device_template.name: Samsung MIM-B19N Modbus interface (DVM / EHS)
device_template.description: Samsung Modbus Interface Module on a DVM/EHS outdoor unit (R1-R2), read over Modbus RTU 9600 8E1. Outdoor block at 0-2, then the indoor unit at address 0 (a hydro kit / EHS, an indoor unit) at 50-79: on/off, mode, set and room temperatures, water in/out, water set point, domestic hot water. Indoor unit N sits at 50 + N*50 + offset (duplicate the rows for more units). The setup steps activate the module's extra values (NASA message ids written to 6000/7000 — a write to the interface module, not a command to the unit). Control registers are written only through the template's Commands (range-checked, spaced 2 s apart, verified by read-back): every write to a holding register is a control command to the unit, so none is enabled until you enable it on the device.
device_template.source_document: Samsung DB68-07538A-03 Installation manual, Modbus Interface Module MIM-B19N/MIM-B19NT, Table 2 (Modbus register table), p. 13-16; the addresses match a Node-RED flow that read the same unit (FC3, address 50 x28). Field-checked 2026-10-08 on a DVM-S with an HE hydro kit at IU 0: 0x7FFF on the hot water temperature = no tank sensor. Extra registers: Table 3 of DB68-07538A-03 (2022) for the official IDs; community IDs from ZimKev's MIM-B19N notes (EHS) and the 'More Hidden Registers' list.

calculated.name: heat_output_estimated
calculated.label: Heat output (estimated)
calculated.expr: water_flow_assumed / 60 * 4.186 * iu0_water_delta_t if compressor_frequency > 0 and iu0_water_delta_t > 0 else 0

calculated.name: power_electric_estimated
calculated.label: Electric power (estimated from the compressor current)

calculated.name: cop_estimated
calculated.label: COP (estimated)
calculated.expr: heat_output_estimated / (first(power_electric, power_electric_estimated) / 1000) if first(power_electric, power_electric_estimated) > 1500 and heat_output_estimated > 0 else 0

calculated.name: low_flow_suspect
calculated.label: Water ΔT over 8 K with the compressor running (low water flow?)

notes.text: Read 0 on a DVM-S with an HE hydro kit (field-checked 2026-10-08), with the compressor running: water flow, pump PWM, room sensor, heater-out and tank temperatures, water-out target, DC link voltage, outdoor fan speed, EVA-in temperature (0x82DE is 'Eva In for EHS') and the experimental energy rows. Why: the HE kit has no flow sensor and switches its water pump on/off (DVM HT/HE installation manual DB68-03973A-06); and these NASA IDs are not in Samsung's list for HE/HT/EHS (MIM manual DB68-07538A-03, Table 3, which names only 0x4087, 0x42F1 and 0x4067) — they come from the community, tested on an EHS system. Each row's description says whether its ID is official or community. On an HE kit, leave these unselected rather than trust a 0; an EHS unit may fill them.

Quiet mode and the compressor limit (FR control, NASA 0x42F1) have no effect on an HE hydro kit: the write is accepted and nothing changes. Samsung documents FR control for hydro units with an integrated tank only.

The values at 4-28 and 82-96 appear only after the setup steps are written (at connect, with writes allowed on the device). A defrost (outdoor_defrost On, step 1-30) after a hard start in cold, humid air is normal.

Heat output is ESTIMATED from the water ΔT and an assumed constant flow, water_flow_assumed (l/min): set it to your circuit's measured flow in the device's Calculated tab (its expression is a plain number). Not the pump's maximum, not Samsung's minimum — an HE kit has no flow sensor and an on/off pump, so the flow is roughly constant while it runs. COP = heat output / electric power, taken from the meter named in Device → Edit → Electricity measured by (power_electric) when there is one, else estimated from the compressor current: √3 × 400 V × I × 0.95 (power_electric_estimated; edit the voltage or the power factor in its expression). The estimate leaves out the fans and the water pump. A heat meter and an electricity meter give the exact COP.

rules.label: Heat pump · on under 25 °C water in, off over 35 °C
rules.description: A buffer thermostat with hysteresis: the unit is switched on when the water returning from the house drops under 25 °C and off only once it is over 35 °C. Between the two nothing changes. At most one switch per 15 minutes, so the compressor is not short-cycled. Change the two temperatures to your system's.

rules.label: Heat pump · lower the water set point while the discharge runs hot
rules.description: Steps on the compressor discharge temperature: over 95 °C the water set point goes to 38 °C, over 100 °C to 35 °C at once; back to your usual set point (normal, 42 °C here) only under 90 °C. A hotter discharge usually means too little water flow or a set point too high for the weather. Set `normal` to your own set point before arming.
